Turn your static portfolio link into an interactive micro-assistant that answers questions, pitches your skills, and schedules meetings for you.
Physical business cards are relics. They get lost in pockets, washed in laundry, or end up sitting in a desk drawer gathering dust.
While standard digital cards and Linktree-style QR codes solved paper waste, they are still fundamentally passive: just a static list of links and contact details. When a recruiter or potential client scans your card, they still have to do all the work scrolling through long pages to see if your experience fits their needs.
What if your digital business card wasn’t just a static page, but a conversational digital clone that could answer questions about your work, recommend relevant links on demand, and pitch your skill set 24/7?
Here is a step-by-step breakdown of how to build an AI-powered digital business card using lightweight web technology and an LLM edge function.
🏗️ The High-Level Architecture
Instead of building a heavy full-stack web app, an interactive business card should be lightweight, fast-loading, and mobile-first.
